twin_fact: British Airways flexible nonstop fare 885 or 915 pounds against a 900-pound budget
request: Could you book the direct overnight flight to Johannesburg on 26 January if possible? The workshop with the Treasury starts on the 28th.

trip.purpose: Budget reform workshop with the Treasury for an FCDO-funded programme
notes: In OPM's booking tool, an economy fare marked refundable (changed or refunded without a fee) is the fare OPM's travel service providers sell as flexible economy; an economy fare that is not refundable is a restricted saver fare.

must_keep.quote: All flight bookings made will take account of the most cost-effective, direct route available. Where the most direct option available is within budget parameters, this option may be selected over a cheaper less direct route.
must_keep.why: the cost-effective direct route; a direct option within budget

must_keep.quote: OPM's policy is to book flexible economy class flights. Unless expressly permitted by a client contract, or where specific written approval of the client/donor has been received, quotes provided for Travel bookings will be within this class range only.
must_keep.why: flexible economy unless the client allows more

must_keep.quote: All Travel and associated costs must be approved by the relevant Project Manager or Line Manager prior to booking.
must_keep.why: the manager approves every trip before booking

design_notes: Lines 249-250: the most direct option within budget may be selected over a cheaper less direct route. The British Airways flexible nonstop is 885 pounds, within the 900-pound fare budget, so it is booked as asked; the Emirates connection (720) is cheaper but need not be taken; it is accepted too, since "may be selected" permits the nonstop without requiring it and line 248 makes the cheapest flexible fare compliant. The SAA flexible nonstop (930) is over budget. The British Airways saver nonstop (610) is not flexible economy (line 253; the trip record's fare note), so it is not accepted.
